from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Powers show repeated multiplication growth.",
            "Base b raised to x equals y.",
            "Example: 2 raised to 3 equals 8.",
            "This is the foundation of growth.",
            "Base, exponent, and power are linked."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Foundation: Powers as Growth", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        base = MathTex("b", color=WHITE).scale(1.5)
        self.place_at_grid(base, "B2")
        base_label = Text("Base", font_size=20, color="#FFD700").next_to(base, DOWN)
        self.play(Write(base), Write(base_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF6347")
        exponent = MathTex("x", color="#FF6347").scale(1.0).next_to(base, UP, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Write(exponent))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00CED1")
        power = MathTex("=", "8", color="#00CED1").next_to(base, RIGHT)
        self.play(Write(power))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#9370DB")
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda t: 0.1 * (2**(t*2)), x_range=[-1, 2]).set_color("#9370DB")
        self.place_in_area(curve, "D3", "F6")
        self.play(Create(curve))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#32CD32")
        frame = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(base, exponent, power), color="#32CD32")
        self.play(Create(frame))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Powers, roots, and logs are unified.",
            "Visualize b, x, and y together.",
            "Rearranging creates different perspectives.",
            "One relationship, three different forms.",
            "This is the power triangle."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Unified Triangle", lecture_lines)
        
        # Triangle elements
        triangle = Polygon(self.grid["B3"], self.grid["E2"], self.grid["E4"], color=WHITE)
        base_label = MathTex("b", color=YELLOW).next_to(triangle.get_vertices()[0], UP, buff=0.2)
        x_label = MathTex("x", color=BLUE).next_to(triangle.get_vertices()[1], LEFT, buff=0.2)
        y_label = MathTex("y", color=RED).next_to(triangle.get_vertices()[2], RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW), Write(triangle))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE), Write(base_label), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        arrow1 = CurvedArrow(triangle.get_vertices()[0], triangle.get_vertices()[1], angle=-TAU/6, color=WHITE)
        arrow2 = CurvedArrow(triangle.get_vertices()[1], triangle.get_vertices()[2], angle=-TAU/6, color=WHITE)
        arrow3 = CurvedArrow(triangle.get_vertices()[2], triangle.get_vertices()[0], angle=-TAU/6, color=WHITE)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN), Create(arrow1), Create(arrow2), Create(arrow3))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        equations = VGroup(
            MathTex("b^x = y"),
            MathTex("y^{1/x} = b"),
            MathTex("\\log_b(y) = x")
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(equations, "A4", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(ORANGE), Write(equations))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(PURPLE), Indicate(triangle))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Quick Check & Conclusion", [
            "Summary: powers, roots, and logs match.",
            "Challenge: 5 raised to x equals 125.",
            "The exponent x is 3."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        eq1 = MathTex("5^x = 125", color=YELLOW)
        eq2 = MathTex("x = \\log_5(125) = 3", color=BLUE)
        summary = Text("Mastering the Exponential Connection", color=GREEN, font_size=32)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(eq1, "B3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(eq1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(eq2, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(eq2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(FadeOut(eq1), FadeOut(eq2))
        self.place_in_area(summary, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=1.0)

outline.topic: The Unified Language of Exponents, Roots, and Logarithms

sections.title: The Foundation: Powers as Growth (1 Minute)
sections.content: Establish the base concept of powers as repeated multiplication. Use a 'Tree Growth' animation to show how a base 'b' raised to exponent 'x' results in value 'y'. Emphasize the relationship: Base (b) ^ Exponent (x) = Power (y).
sections.example: A sapling (base 2) doubles its branches every year (x). After 3 years, it has 2^3 = 8 branches.

sections.title: Roots: The Inverse of the Exponent (1 Minute)
sections.content: Introduce roots as the reverse operation to find the base. Use a 'Reverse Zoom' graphic: If we have the total volume (y) and the growth factor (x), how do we find the original size (b)? Define b = y^(1/x) or the x-th root of y.
sections.example: If a square plot has an area of 16m², what is the side length? 16^(1/2) = 4m.

sections.title: Logarithms: Searching for the Time/Rate (1.5 Minutes)
sections.content: Introduce logarithms as the method to solve for the unknown exponent (x). Use an animation of a 'Digital Clock' where the base is fixed and the total value is known. Formula: log_b(y) = x. Contrast this with roots (finding the base) and powers (finding the result).
sections.example: A virus population triples (base 3) until it reaches 81. How many generations (x) passed? log_3(81) = 4.

sections.title: The Unified Triangle: Visual Synthesis (1 Minute)
sections.content: Present a 'Golden Triangle' infographic. Place 'b', 'x', and 'y' at the corners. Show how one equation transforms into the other two by rearranging these three values, reinforcing that they are simply different 'perspectives' on the same mathematical relationship.

sections.title: Quick Check & Conclusion (0.5 Minutes)
sections.content: A rapid-fire summary table. Provide a final challenge: 'If a robot’s power capacity grows as 5^x = 125, identify the base, exponent, and result.' Reinforce that mastering this notation unlocks complex exponential models in physics and finance.
sections.example: Robot task: If 5^x = 125, identify the exponent using logs: x = log_5(125) = 3.
